source_text: Ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐᾷ τοῦτον, ὥς φασι, διαφθαρῆναι ἡ φήνη· ἀλλ' ὑπολαβοῦσα αὐτὸν τοῖς οἰκείοις ἑαυτῆς νεοσσοῖς συνεκτρέφει. Τοιοῦτοι, τῶν γονέων, οἱ ἐπὶ προφάσει πενίας ἐκτιθέμενοι τὰ νήπια· ἢ καὶ ἐν τῇ διανομῇ τοῦ κλήρου ἀνισότατοι πρὸς τὰ ἔκγονα. Δίκαιον γὰρ, ὥσπερ ἐξ ἴσου μεταδεδώκασιν ἑκάστῳ τοῦ εἶναι, οὕτω καὶ τὰς πρὸς τὸ ζῆν ἀφορμὰς ἴσως αὐτοῖς καὶ ὁμοτίμως παρέχειν. Μὴ μιμήσῃ τῶν γαμψωνύχων ὀρνίθων τὸ ἀπηνές· οἳ ἐπειδὰν ἴδωσι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεοττοὺς κατατολμῶντας λοιπὸν τῆς πτήσεως, ἐκβάλλουσι τῆς καλιᾶς, τύπ τοντες τοῖς πτεροῖς καὶ ὠθοῦντες, καὶ οὐδεμίαν ἐπιμέλειαν ποιοῦνται πρὸς τὸ λοιπόν. Ἐπαινετὸν τῆς κορώνης τὸ φιλότεκνον· ἣ καὶ πετομένων ἤδη παρέπεται, σιτίζουσα αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐκτρέφουσα μέχρι πλείστου. Πολλὰ τῶν ὀρνίθων γένη οὐδὲν πρὸς τὴν κύησιν δεῖται τῆς τῶν ἀρρένων ἐπιπλοκῆς· ἀλλ' ἐν μὲν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἄγονά ἐστι τὰ ὑπηνέμια, τοὺς δὲ γύπας φασὶν ἀσυνδυάστως τίκτειν ὡς τὰ πολλὰ, καὶ ταῦτα μακροβιωτάτους ὄντας· οἷς γε μέχρις ἑκατὸν ἐτῶν, ὡς τὰ πολλὰ, παρατείνεται ἡ ζωή. Τοῦτό μοι ἔχε παρασεσημειωμένον ἐκ τῆς περὶ τοὺς ὄρνιθας ἱστορίας, ἵν' ἐπειδάν ποτε ἴδῃς γελῶντάς τινας τὸ μυστήριον ἡμῶν, ὡς ἀδυνάτου ὄντος καὶ ἔξω τῆς φύσεως, παρθένον τεκεῖν, τῆς παρθενίας αὐτῆς φυλαττομένης ἀχράντου, ἐνθυμηθῇς ὅτι ὁ εὐδοκήσας ἐν τῇ μωρίᾳ τοῦ κηρύγματος σῶσαι τοὺς πιστεύοντας, μυρίας ἐκ τῆς φύσεως ἀφορμὰς πρὸς τὴν πίστιν τῶν παραδόξων προλαβὼν κατεβάλετο. 8.7 Ἐξαγαγέτω τὰ ὕδατα ἑρπετὰ ψυχῶν ζωσῶν, καὶ πετεινὰ πετόμενα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, κατὰ τὸ στερέωμα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. Ἐπὶ μὲν τῆς γῆς ἐκελεύσθη πετάσθαι, διὰ τὸ πᾶσι τὴν τροφὴν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ὑπάρχειν· Κατὰ δὲ τὸ στερέωμα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὡς προλαβόντες ἀποδεδώκαμεν, οὐρανοῦ ἐνταῦθα παρὰ τὸ ὁρᾶσθαι τοῦ ἀέρος προσειρημένου· στερεώματος δὲ, διὰ τὸ πυκνότερόν πως εἶναι, συγκρίσει τοῦ αἰθερίου σώματος, καὶ μᾶλλον πεπιλημένον ταῖς κάτωθεν ἀναφοραῖς τὸν ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς ἡμῶν ἀέρα. Ἔχεις οὖν οὐρανὸν διακεκοσμημένον, γῆν κεκαλλωπισμένην, θάλασαν εὐθηνουμένην τοῖς οἰκείοις γεννήμασιν, ἀέρα πλήρη τῶν διιπταμένων αὐτὸν ὀρνίθων. Πάντα προστάγματι Θεοῦ ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι παραχθέντα, καὶ ὅσα ὁ λόγος παρῆκε νῦν, τὴν ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἐν τούτοις διατριβὴν ἐκκλίνων, ὡς ἂν μὴ δόξῃ ὑπερεκπίπτειν τοῦ μέτρου, κατὰ σεαυτὸν συλ λογισάμενος, ὅγε φιλόπονος, τὴν ἐν ἅπασι τοῦ Θεοῦ σοφίαν καταμανθάνων, μὴ λήξῃς ποτὲ τοῦ θαύματος, μηδὲ τοῦ διὰ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως δοξάζειν τὸν ποιητήν. Ἔχεις ἐν τῷ σκότει τὰ νυκτερόβια γένη τῶν ὀρνίθων· ἐν τῷ φωτὶ τὰ ἡμερόφοιτα. Νυκτερίδες μὲν γὰρ, καὶ γλαῦκες, καὶ νυκτο κόρακες, τῶν νυκτινόμων εἰσίν. Ὥστε σοί ποτε ἐν καιρῷ μὴ παρόντος τοῦ ὕπνου, ἐξαρκεῖν καὶ τὴν ἐν τούτοις διατριβὴν, καὶ τὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτοῖς ἰδιωμάτων ἐξέτασιν πρὸς δοξολογίαν τοῦ ποιητοῦ. Πῶς ἄγρυπνον ἡ ἀηδὼν, ὅταν ἐπωάζῃ, διὰ πάσης νυκτὸς τῆς μελῳδίας μὴ ἀπολήγουσα. Πῶς τετράπουν τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πτηνὸν ἡ νυκτερίς. Πῶς μόνη τῶν ὀρνίθων ὀδοῦσι κέχρηται, καὶ ζωογονεῖ μὲν ὡς τὰ τετράποδα, ἐπιπολάζει δὲ τῷ ἀέρι, οὐχὶ πτερῷ κουφιζομένη, ἀλλ' ὑμένι τινὶ δερματίνῳ.
thought_title: Birds as moral examples and the fifth day command
orientation: Basil is still expounding the moral lessons from birds, then moves to the fifth day of creation when God commands the waters to bring forth living creatures and birds.
pass_a_gloss: But the vulture, they say, does not allow this one to be destroyed; but taking it up, it rears it together with its own chicks. Such are, among parents, those who expose their infants on the pretext of poverty; or also in the division of the inheritance most unjust toward their offspring. For it is right that, just as they have given to each equally a share of being, so also to provide the means for living to them equally and with equal honor. Do not imitate the cruelty of the taloned birds; who, whenever they see their own chicks now daring flight, cast them out of the nest, striking with wings and pushing, and make no further care for the rest. Praiseworthy is the crow's love of offspring; which follows along even when they are already flying, feeding them and rearing them until the greatest extent. Many kinds of birds need no intercourse with males for conception; but among the others the wind-eggs are infertile, but vultures, they say, give birth without pairing for the most part, and these are very long-lived; for whom life extends, for the most part, up to a hundred years. Hold this noted for me from the history concerning birds, so that whenever you see some people laughing at our mystery, as if it were impossible and outside nature for a virgin to give birth while her virginity is kept undefiled, you may remember that the one who was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe, took in advance countless starting points from nature for faith in the paradoxes and laid them down. 8.7 Let the waters bring forth creeping things of living souls, and winged creatures flying upon the earth, along the firmament of heaven. Upon the earth it was commanded to fly, because food for all comes from the earth; but along the firmament of heaven, as we have previously explained, heaven here is spoken of because the air is seen; and firmament, because the air above our head is somehow denser, in comparison with the ethereal body, and more compressed by the exhalations from below. You have therefore heaven adorned, earth beautified, sea flourishing with its own offspring, air full of the birds that fly through it. All things by the command of God were brought from not being into being, and as many things as the discourse has now passed over, avoiding the longer dwelling on these, so that it may not seem to exceed the measure, you yourself having reasoned, you who are industrious, learning thoroughly the wisdom of God in all things, may you never cease from wonder, nor from glorifying the maker through all creation. You have in the darkness the night-roaming kinds of birds; in the light the day-wandering ones. For bats, and owls, and night-ravens are among the night-dwelling ones. So that for you at some time, when sleep is not present, the dwelling on these is sufficient, and the examination of the properties belonging to them, for the glorification of the maker. How sleepless is the nightingale, when it sits on eggs, not ceasing from melody through the whole night. How the bat is the same both four-footed and winged. How alone of birds it uses teeth, and brings forth live young as the four-footed animals, and moves over the air, not lifted by a wing, but by a certain membrane of skin.

lemmas.gloss: vulture (specifically the lammergeier or osprey-like bird)

choices.why: The context contrasts with the eagle's rejection of its chick; φήνη is a bird of prey that adopts the abandoned chick, best rendered as vulture in English
The term refers to unfertilized eggs produced without male intercourse; 'wind-eggs' preserves the literal sense of eggs produced by wind alone

choices.english: through the foolishness of the proclamation
choices.why: This echoes Paul's language in 1 Corinthians about the foolishness of preaching; 'proclamation' renders κήρυγμα as the act of preaching
rejected: through the folly of the message

choices.why: This is the literal LXX wording from Genesis 1:20; 'living souls' preserves the Greek ψυχῶν ζωσῶν rather than smoothing to 'living creatures'
The compound means 'living by night'; 'night-roaming' captures the active sense of βίος as manner of life

choices.english: by a certain membrane of skin
choices.why: The literal rendering preserves Basil's precise anatomical description of the bat's wing as a skin membrane rather than feathers

pass_b_english: But the vulture, they say, does not allow it to perish. It takes the chick up and rears it together with its own young. Such are those parents who expose their infants on the pretext of poverty, or who are most unfair to their offspring in the division of an inheritance. For it is right that, just as they have given each one a share in being equally, so they should provide the means for living to them equally and with equal honor. Do not imitate the cruelty of the birds with curved talons. When they see their young now daring to fly, they drive them out of the nest, striking them with their wings and pushing them, and they take no further care of them. The love of the crow for its young is praiseworthy: it accompanies them even when they are already flying, feeding them and rearing them for a very long time. Many kinds of birds need no intercourse with males for conception. In other birds the wind-eggs are infertile, but they say that vultures for the most part give birth without pairing, and these are very long-lived; their life extends for the most part to a hundred years. Keep this noted down for yourself from the study of birds, so that whenever you see people laughing at our mystery, as though it were impossible and outside nature for a virgin to give birth while her virginity remains undefiled, you may remember that the One who was pleased to save those who believe through the foolishness of the proclamation (1 Corinthians 1:21) prepared in advance countless starting points from nature for faith in things beyond expectation. "Let the waters bring forth creeping things of living souls, and winged creatures flying upon the earth, across the firmament of heaven" (Genesis 1:20). They were commanded to fly upon the earth because food for all comes from the earth. And "across the firmament of heaven," as we have already explained, because the air is here called "heaven" from being seen, and "firmament" because the air above our heads is somehow denser in comparison with the ethereal body, and more compressed by the exhalations from below. You have, then, a heaven adorned, an earth beautified, a sea teeming with its own offspring, an air full of the birds that fly through it. All things were brought by the command of God from non-being into being. And whatever the discourse has now passed over, avoiding a longer dwelling on these matters so as not to seem to exceed its measure, you who love labor should reason out for yourself, learning the wisdom of God in all things, and never cease from wonder, nor from glorifying the Maker through all creation. You have in the darkness the night-roaming kinds of birds; in the light, those that go about by day. Bats, owls, and night-ravens are among the night-dwellers. So when sleep is not present at some time, it is enough for you to spend time on these things and to examine the properties they possess for the glorification of the Maker. How sleepless the nightingale is when she sits on her eggs, not ceasing from her song through the whole night. How the bat is at once four-footed and winged. How it alone among birds uses teeth, and gives birth to live young like four-footed animals, and floats upon the air, not lifted by a wing, but by a certain membrane of skin.

problems.quote: moves over the air, not lifted by a feather, but by a certain membrane of skin
problems.source_quote: ἐπιπολάζει δὲ τῷ ἀέρι, οὐχὶ πτερῷ κουφιζομένη, ἀλλ' ὑμένι τινὶ δερματίνῳ
problems.why: ἐπιπολάζει means 'floats/skims upon', not 'moves over'; and πτερῷ is 'wing' (by a wing), not 'a feather'. The bat is not lifted by a wing but by a membrane.
problems.fix: and floats upon the air, not lifted by a wing, but by a certain membrane of skin
problems.ruling: πτερῷ = 'wing' not 'a feather'; ἐπιπολάζει = 'floats on' not 'moves over'. 'A feather' misleads readers about bat anatomy.

edits.old: moves over the air, not lifted by a feather, but by a certain membrane of skin
edits.new: floats upon the air, not lifted by a wing, but by a certain membrane of skin

fixed: Corrected 'moves over the air, not lifted by a feather' to 'floats upon the air, not lifted by a wing': source has ἐπιπολάζει ('floats/skims upon') and πτερῷ ('wing').

last_rejected.why: φήνη is the she-eagle, not vulture; wrong bird species changes the natural history claim.
last_rejected.fix: But the eagle, they say, does not allow it to perish.
last_rejected.ruling: φήνη can mean vulture or eagle; LSJ cites Aristophanes for vulture. Within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: γαμψώνυχες specifically means birds of prey/hawks, not generic 'birds with curved talons'; natural history point lost.
last_rejected.fix: Do not imitate the cruelty of the hawks.
last_rejected.ruling: γαμψώνυχος = curved-taloned; 'birds with curved talons' is literal and accurate. Mere preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: γύπες are vultures, but earlier φήνη was mistranslated as 'vulture'; now two different birds are conflated.
last_rejected.fix: but they say that vultures for the most part give birth without pairing
last_rejected.ruling: γύψ = vulture is correct; φήνη also rendered vulture is defensible. No conflation if φήνη can mean vulture.

last_rejected.why: ὑπηνέμια are wind-eggs (unfertilized eggs), not 'wind-eggs are infertile'—the point is they don't produce offspring, not that the eggs themselves are 'infertile' as a quality; but more critically, the contrast is between other birds' wind-eggs being barren vs. vultures reproducing without mating.
last_rejected.fix: In other birds the wind-eggs are barren
last_rejected.ruling: ἄγονα = unproductive/infertile; 'infertile' for wind-eggs is accurate. Contrast preserved. Not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ἀηδών is nightingale—correct. But 'How sleepless the nightingale is when she sits on her eggs'—ἄγρυπνον = 'wakeful/sleepless,' correct. However, 'sits on her eggs' = ἐπωάζῃ, which is 'broods/incubates'—correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms all renderings correct. No problem exists.
